clue.text: Heartless sheep dog

indicators.note: heartless means the word sheep loses the letter at its centre

explanation.surface: A cruel remark about a sheep, or a callous sheepdog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle E of SHEEP. Shep was the Blue Peter dog, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Shep is a classic name for a collie, and the famous Blue Peter pet was a Border collie.

clue.text: Sad broadcaster leaves upset and emotional originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the words broadcaster, leaves, upset and emotional

explanation.surface: A broadcaster walks out of the studio, shaken and tearful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of broadcaster, leaves, upset and emotional; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or down in spirits is a common informal synonym meaning unhappy.

clue.text: A guide's composed about new part of the liturgy

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters sit around the next piece
composed means the letters of a guide's are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A guide has written something concerning a fresh section of the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges A GUIDES, and 'about' puts that around N for new.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei ('Lamb of God') is a fixed prayer sung or said in the Mass.

clue.text: Russian physiologist taking the base from meringue cake

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom letter, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a pavlova is a meringue dessert topped with fruit and cream

explanation.surface: A Russian scientist removing the bottom from a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the 'base' is the last letter, so 'taking the base from' drops the final A of PAVLOVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov was the Russian scientist famous for conditioned reflexes in dogs.

clue.text: Sullen upper class girl stands up swindler

parts.note: a black mood is a sullen one, so black can mean sullen

indicators.note: stands up in a down clue means the piece is written from bottom to top

parts.note: gel is the posh pronunciation of girl, used for an upper-class girl

explanation.surface: A moody posh girl stands up a conman, leaving him waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands up' reverses GEL to LEG in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackleg is an old term for a cheat or sharper, especially at the racecourse or card table.

clue.text: Do part of housework with a small word of encouragement

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
hup is a cry urging on a horse or marching soldiers

explanation.surface: Doing a household chore while someone offers a little cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning the dishes after a meal is a standard household chore.

clue.text: High pitched river conflict

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a set-to is a fight or argument

explanation.surface: A shrill argument breaking out by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto voice is an artificially high one, above the singer's natural range.

clue.text: Proposal to put short leather strip in front of dress shirt

indicators.note: to put signals the following piece being placed somewhere, completed by in
in says where it goes: inside the proposal word

parts.note: a plan is a proposal or scheme

indicators.note: short means the leather-strip word loses its final letter

parts.note: a strop is a leather strap for sharpening razors

explanation.surface: A suggestion to add a small leather trim to the front of a formal shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'to put ... in' is split by the piece it moves; 'short' drops the last letter of the strop.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastron is the stiffened panel on the chest of a formal shirt.

clue.text: Cherished ambition of Hillary to dance with old German leader

indicators.note: to dance means the letters move about into a new arrangement
the leader of German is its first letter

explanation.surface: Hillary dancing with an aged German head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dance' rearranges HILLARY with O (old) and G, the first letter picked by 'leader' from German.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grail of legend has come to stand for any long-sought, highly prized goal.

clue.text: Benefit of a yashmak, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is said out loud and matched by sound

parts.note: a yashmak is a veil worn by some Muslim women, so a yashmak is a veil

explanation.surface: Someone questioning the advantages of wearing a yashmak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says 'a veil' aloud, giving a word of the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of no avail is to be of no use, so avail means advantage or use.

clue.text: Maybe Prometheus has quiet dance embracing queen

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: embracing means the dance word wraps around the queen piece

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A Greek Titan doing a quiet jig around a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks an example: Prometheus (2012) was Ridley Scott's film set before Alien.
explanation.definitionFit: The film Prometheus tells an earlier story leading up to the original Alien film.

clue.text: Be excited about earl's old rifle

indicators.note: about means the excited word goes round the earl's letter

parts.note: to rave is to talk wildly or enthuse
E is an abbreviation for earl; the 's links on to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by an aristocrat's antique gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' is the verb meaning plunder, not the gun; reave is an archaic word, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reave is an archaic verb for to plunder or rob, the sense of rifle through.

clue.text: Commanding officer accommodates Lesley Judd and others?

parts.note: to host guests is to accommodate them

explanation.surface: An officer puts up a TV presenter and her friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Lesley Judd was one of several Blue Peter presenters working alongside each other, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenters who share a show are joint presenters, one of a team fronting it together.

clue.text: Madcap designated driver travelling with Valerie

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving around into a new order

explanation.surface: A sober chauffeur on a trip with a woman named Valerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges DD with VALERIE. Valerie Singleton was another Blue Peter presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, wild person who takes dangerous risks for thrills is a madcap.

clue.text: Look closely around opening of the safe

indicators.note: around means the looking word surrounds the next letter

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

indicators.note: opening of takes just the first letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A safecracker inspecting the door of a strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' looks like part of the scene but is the definition: peter is old criminal slang for a safe. 'around' puts PEER round T from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter is underworld slang for a strongbox, as in a peterman who blows them open.

clue.text: Joyful element seaside town curtailed

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, an element

indicators.note: curtailed means the town name loses its last letter

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall

explanation.surface: Something about a seaside resort is cut short, yet still cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives is a Cornish seaside town; 'curtailed' cuts its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive describes a merry, celebratory mood, as at holiday time.

clue.text: Cheer properly — "Toodle-pip"

parts.note: cheer in the old sense of food and drink, as in good cheer, is fare
well means properly or in a proper way

explanation.surface: A jolly send-off with a cheery British goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Toodle-pip is an old-fashioned British way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye, toodle-pip being jaunty dated British slang.

clue.text: Dance group supports South American artist

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports others sits beneath them

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A band backing a painter from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts BAND underneath SA and RA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The saraband is a stately Spanish court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Risk public appearance

definitions.meaning: publicity or being seen in the media

explanation.surface: The hazard of showing your face in public.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both vulnerability to danger and being shown before the public.

clue.text: Alight to pick up party opponents

parts.note: to get something is to pick it up or fetch it
a do is a party
in bridge West and North sit at adjacent seats and are opponents

explanation.surface: Arriving to collect rivals from a party.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, players sitting West and North are on opposing sides, so W and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight from a bus or horse is to step off, descend from it.

clue.text: Support corporation describing beginning of trend over finger spinner

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around, so the outer pieces enclose the rest

parts.note: a tee is a golf ball's support
corporation is jocular for a big belly, a tum

indicators.note: beginning of takes the first letter of the word trend

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A company backing a new craze for fidget spinners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing round, so the support and the belly together enclose the T and the O. A corporation is old jocular slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotum is a small spinning top twirled with the fingers, often with lettered sides.

clue.text: Used to be holding husband in which position?

indicators.note: holding means the past-tense verb contains the next letter

parts.note: were is a past form of be
H is the abbreviation for husband in family trees

explanation.surface: Wondering where a married man once stood.
explanation.definitionFit: The interrogative asking at what place or location something is.

clue.text: Back peacekeepers to abandon a further appearance

indicators.note: to abandon means the back word drops the letter given by a

parts.note: the rear is the back
UN peacekeepers are United Nations forces

explanation.surface: Supporting UN troops pulling out of a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' removes A from REAR, leaving RER.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat showing of a programme is another broadcast, its showing again.

clue.text: See 28
Master of ceremonies attending leading lady

parts.note: to be present is to be attending
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the country's leading lady

explanation.surface: A compere turning up at a star actress's side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading lady' is not an actress here but the Queen, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere or host introducing acts on stage or on TV is the show's MC.

clue.text: Maybe those who take tiffin without bits of butter

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
pats are small portions of butter

explanation.surface: People having afternoon tea with no butter on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiffin is a light meal in British India, taken by colonial Britons abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: British people living in India, notably in the Raj, were emigrants who took the light lunch called tiffin.

clue.text: Plots to include computer-aided manufacturing in IT devices

indicators.note: to include means the plots word takes the manufacturing letters inside

parts.note: a web is an intricate plot or snare, as in a web of deceit
CAM is the standard abbreviation for computer-aided manufacturing

explanation.surface: Schemes to bring factory automation into computer hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cameras that stream video over the internet are common computer peripherals.

clue.text: Support Japanese and French aircraft

parts.note: a prop is a support
et is French for and

explanation.surface: Backing a Franco-Japanese aviation project.
explanation.definitionFit: A turboprop plane, a jet engine driving propellers, is a type of aeroplane.

clue.text: Little woman badly shaken on becoming 14 2 15 24

parts.note: Jo March is a heroine of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women

indicators.note: badly means the letters of shaken on are jumbled

explanation.surface: A small woman rattled after a transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SHAKENON. The cross-reference reads DAREDEVIL BLUE PETER PRESENTER: John Noakes was famous for his stunts on the BBC children's show Blue Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: Noakes was the Blue Peter host known for death-defying stunts, such as climbing Nelson's Column.

clue.text: On reflection change the course of events

indicators.note: reflection as in a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to edit is to change text

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, someone decides to alter what happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide of events is the general drift or trend of how things are going.

clue.text: Gymnastic movement with long rope

definitions.meaning: a forward thrust with one leg bent, as in fencing or exercise
a ... or ... line is a long rein used to exercise a horse in circles

explanation.surface: A gymnast's routine performed with a long rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a forward exercise thrust and a long training rein for horses.

clue.text: Improved detail in part of musical instrument

indicators.note: in means the detail word sits inside the instrument word

parts.note: a reed is the vibrating part of an oboe or clarinet
a touch is a small detail or finishing stroke

explanation.surface: A small detail added to part of an oboe.
explanation.definitionFit: Retouched work such as a photo has been touched up, enhanced with small corrections.
